decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display stays close to the cardboard core and is cheap to carry, but its absence from the website in 2020 to 2021 and the 2022 paper and energy cost squeeze make a catalog clean-up more likely than in 2019.

The pegboard-back variant uses existing capacity for hook merchandise, yet its lack of visibility since 2019 and cost-driven problemistic search raise the risk that it gets folded back into the standard line.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a staple format that most likely meets aspirations and anchors the one-stop offer, so it is kept even under cost pressure.
The eighth-pallet format complements the quarter-pallet line at low incremental cost, though its missing presence after 2019 suggests some risk of consolidation.

The wooden pallet lies further from the cardboard core, suffered from the 2021 to 2022 timber price spike and from four years without visible traction, so a shortfall against aspiration points to redirecting resources to the core business.

Demand for media-product displays is structurally declining, and after the COVID retail disruption and rising input costs this shortfall triggers problemistic search, so the resources go back to core display formats.
